title: Patch: one press of End turn or a one-tap answer sends once, so a double click can't end an extra turn

**Issue #3060 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #3060: Patch: one press of End turn or a one-tap answer sends once, so a double click can't end an extra turn
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Online and in practice, the board waits a moment for the game's answer after you press End turn. Until that answer arrives the button still works, so a double click sends End turn twice. Usually the second one is refused, and a red "it is not your turn" line sits on the board for the whole of the opponent's turn. But when the card you played gave you an extra turn, the second End turn is accepted and ends the extra turn before you have seen it. A double tap on a one-tap choice does the same thing. Once this is built, a repeat of the same End turn or answer against the same board is dropped.

## Why

- `apps/web/src/game/Game.tsx:541`: `const legal = shown === view ? offered : NOTHING_LEGAL;` keeps the shown view's moves live until a new view arrives, and `dispatch` (:545-551) sends every call.
- `apps/web/src/game/Board.tsx:666-675`: `pressEndTurn` sets `pressedFor` and calls `onControl("end-turn")`, but never checks `pressed` (:605) first. The button only "stays visibly depressed" (:520).
- `apps/web/src/game/Prompt.tsx:1255-1259`: an immediate pick calls `send([key])` with no check that it was already sent.
- `apps/web/src/game/net.ts:847`: every send gets a fresh nonce, so the engine's nonce dedupe never sees the repeat.
- Extra turns are taken when the turn ends (`crates/engine/src/state.rs:1391`, `extra_turns`, R846). The player is still the active one, so the second End turn is legal. Event Horizon (`stinkyscape/c004_3_event_horizon.rs`) and Temporal Rift (`meditative/c019_1_temporal_rift.rs`) grant extra turns.

## Proposal

- In `Game.tsx`'s `dispatch`, remember the last `endTurn`, `answer` or `mulligan` body sent and the `view` object it was sent against, and drop an equal body sent against the same view.
- A new view, or a change of the `error` prop (a refused or offline send), clears that memory so a retry goes through.
- Leave concede, auto end turn, plays, activations and market buys alone: a repeat of those can be intended, and the engine refuses what it must. This only collapses a duplicate intent against one view and enforces no rule (CLAUDE.md rule 7).
- A ruling note for the behaviour, a test named after it, and its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/<issue>.md`.

## Where it lands

- `apps/web/src/game/Game.tsx` and `Game.test.tsx`.
- `apps/web/README.md` (the board's dispatch).
- `spec/rulings/` and `spec/pending/` (§10.10).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two End turn clicks against one view send one `endTurn`. After a new view, a third click sends.
- [ ] A changed `error` prop releases the guard, so End turn sends again after a refusal or after going offline.
- [ ] A double-tapped one-tap choice sends one `answer`, and a double-pressed mulligan Ready sends one `mulligan`.
- [ ] Concede and plays are never dropped.
- [ ] Hotseat, whose views arrive at once, behaves as it does today.

## Size and risks

Small: about 40 lines in one module, plus tests and a ruling note. The risk is an accepted action that brings no new view, which would block an identical retry. Releasing the guard on any error and on any new view covers refusals and offline sends.

   // against the same view is a repeat press, dropped; a new view is a new object, so it needs no clearing.
   const lastSent = useRef<{ key: string; view: PlayerView } | null>(null);

   useLayoutEffect(() => {
     if (error != null && error !== "") lastSent.current = null;
   }, [error]);

     (body: ActionBody) => {

         const key = JSON.stringify(body);
         const sent = lastSent.current;
         if (sent !== null && sent.view === latest.current && sent.key === key) return;

       onAction(body);
     },

   );

- Regression (the existing suites that click End turn or answer prompts): `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/game src/test/ux src/routes/match.test.tsx src/routes/practice.test.tsx src/routes/practice-tutorial.test.tsx src/duos src/tutorial`

- [ ] Two End turn clicks on one view send one `endTurn`; after a new view a further click sends (test 1).
- [ ] An `error` that gains text releases the guard; the error clearing does not (test 2).
- [ ] A double-tapped one-tap choice sends one `answer`, and a double-pressed Ready sends one `mulligan` (tests 3 and 4).
- [ ] Concede and attacks are never dropped, and a hotseat-style board is unchanged (tests 5 and 6).
- [ ] The existing web suites in the regression command above pass.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and eslint on the two files pass.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh spec check` passes, with R3060000's note, its pending paragraph and the §10.10 link in place.
- [ ] No `.skip`, `eslint-disable`, `@ts-ignore` or new `#[allow]` was added, and nothing under `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/` or `bot/` changed.
- [ ] The harness checks pass: `rustfmt`, `catalog`, `patches`, `rulings`, `clippy`, the cargo tests (no wire diff), and the web tests with `--changed origin/main`.

## Risks

- **A stale error line defeating the guard.** `net.ts` `send` sets `error` to null before every send, and `ack` clears it. Releasing on any change of `error`, as the issue proposes, would let click 2 through whenever an old refusal was on screen. Step 3 releases only when the error is non-empty. Test 2 pins this.
- **An accepted action that brings no new view would block an identical retry.**
  - Online, every accepted action broadcasts a new view object, and a refusal arrives as an `error` frame.
  - In practice, each snapshot's view is a new object.
  - A reconnect's first view is new too.
  - The one gap is an offline send repeated with the same error text: `error` does not change, so the next identical press is dropped until the reconnect's fresh view. That press would have been refused anyway.
- **Different answers against one view still go through**, since only an equal body is dropped, as the issue says. The engine refuses a stale answer.
- **Hidden information and replay.** None is touched. The guard works on the body and the view object's identity only, nonces and the wire are unchanged, and no engine or server code changes.
- **Duos and the lessons.** Both reuse `Game`'s `dispatch`. Their views are new objects per frame or snapshot, so the same release rules apply. Run the regression command to confirm.

## Decisions the task did not settle

- The guard releases on an `error` that becomes non-empty, not on any change. Rejected: the issue's literal "any change", for the stale-error reason above.
- The guard key is `latest.current`, the newest `view` prop, not `shown`. This keeps `dispatch`'s deps at `[onAction]` and also covers a double tap during an animation hold. Rejected: adding `shown` to the deps.
- The release is a `useLayoutEffect`, as the nearby view-seen effect is, so it is in place before the next click. Rejected: `useEffect`, which can lag a click by one frame.
- The equality is `JSON.stringify(body)`. Bodies come from the same builders each time, so key order is stable.

## Open questions

None.
````
